cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend, because this one starts heavy. John the Baptist has been beheaded in prison, and his disciples have gone and told Jesus (Matthew 14:10-12). When Jesus hears about John, He withdraws by boat privately to a solitary place.

cards.question: When the crowds find out that Jesus has gone off by boat to a solitary place, they stay put in their towns.

cards.text: Jesus steps ashore, and there it is, a LARGE crowd.

cards.question: Jesus went looking for a solitary place and found a large crowd. How does He respond to them?

answers.text: He sends them back to their towns
He sails off to another shore

cards.question: When Jesus steps ashore and sees the large crowd, He ___ their sick.

cards.text: Evening comes, and the disciples tell Jesus it's a desolate place and the hour is already late. You can hear a plan coming.

cards.question: It's late and they're in a desolate place. What do the disciples want Jesus to do with the crowds?

answers.text: Send them to the villages to buy food
Keep them here to camp for the night
Have them fish along the shore

cards.text: Honestly, sending everybody off to buy food sounds sensible, and I'd sign off on it myself. “They do not need to go away,” Jesus replies.

cards.question: If the crowds aren't going anywhere, who does Jesus say should give them something to eat?

cards.text: So the disciples check what they've got, and friend, I bet I know this feeling. One little bag of chocolate chips, an order for a thousand cookie boxes, and me staring at that bag like it owes me money.

cards.question: What do the disciples tell Jesus they have for the whole crowd?

answers.text: Only five loaves and two fish
Only seven loaves and a few fish
Only two loaves and one fish

cards.text: Jesus has one answer for that count. “Bring them here to Me,” He says.

cards.question: Before anything is handed out, Jesus directs the crowds to sit down on the grass.
Jesus takes the five loaves and the two fish, looks up to ___ and speaks a blessing.

cards.text: Then He breaks the loaves and gives them to the disciples, and the disciples give them to the people. Five loaves, two fish, a LARGE crowd, and you see where my eyebrows are going.

cards.question: When it's all done, the people in the crowd all ___ and were ___.

cards.text: Then the disciples pick up what's left over. Friend, not ONCE in all my batches have I ended up with more than I started with, and if it ever happens, I'm framing it.

cards.question: How many basketfuls of broken pieces do the disciples pick up?
About five thousand men were fed, and that count doesn't include the women and children.
